text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text, such as books, websites, and articles. To get good results, users often use prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs can answer questions, translate languages, and help with writing. However, they also have limits. They sometimes make mistakes or give outdated information because they only know what was in their training data. They cannot truly think or feel, so users should always check important facts.
